records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.1: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me: the oracle of the end
decisions.reason: The heading of 3:16 and 6:1 introduces chapter 7, a message about "the end". Its short, urgent clauses and repeated cries are close to poetry, but the chapter is set as prose here, as most of Ezekiel is.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (L); The word of the LORD came to me: (B); The LORD gave me this message: (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 6:1. The oracle that follows takes no quotation marks, by the rule set for Ezekiel.

records.heading: The end has come

records.source: וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן־אָדָ֗ם כֹּה־אָמַ֞ר אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה לְאַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל קֵ֑ץ בָּ֣א הַקֵּ֔ץ עַל־אַרְבַּ֖ע כַּנְפ֥וֹת הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: And you, son of man, thus says [the] Lord Yahweh to [the] land of Israel: An end! Has come the end on [the] four corners of the land.
pieces: Son of man, the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this to the land of Israel: An end! The end has come to the four corners of the land.

L.2: And you, son of man, thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} to the land of Israel: An end! The end has come upon the four edges of the land.

R.2: Son of man, this is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says about the land of Israel: The end! The end has come to every part of the land.

decisions.choice: An end! The end has come: Amos 8:2
decisions.reason: The LORD told Amos, "The end has come upon my people Israel" (Amos 8:2), with a play on the words for "summer fruit" and "end". Ezekiel takes up Amos's word and repeats it again and again (verses 2, 3, 6): what Amos announced for the northern kingdom has now come for the whole land. The end is the end of the nation as it was, not the end of the world.

decisions.choice: the four corners of the land: the whole land
decisions.reason: The four corners are the four edges or ends of the land, in every direction (Isaiah 11:12). Nowhere will be spared. The word "four" is written in a slightly different spelling from the one the scribes' marginal note gives; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: verses 2-9: the order of the Hebrew
decisions.reason: The Greek translation gives verses 3-9 in a different order and is shorter in places in this chapter. The Hebrew order is followed. Verses 3-4 and 8-9 are near repetitions of each other, like a refrain.

decisions.choice: thus says the Lord GOD / the Lord GOD says this / this is what the Lord GOD says
decisions.reason: The formula as set at 2:4. Readable says "every part of the land" for "the four corners" (m2).

records.source: עַתָּה֙ הַקֵּ֣ץ עָלַ֔יִךְ וְשִׁלַּחְתִּ֤י אַפִּי֙ בָּ֔ךְ וּשְׁפַטְתִּ֖יךְ כִּדְרָכָ֑יִךְ וְנָתַתִּ֣י עָלַ֔יִךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־תּוֹעֲבֹתָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: Now the end [is] on you, and I will send my anger against you, and I will judge you according to your ways, and I will lay on you all your abominations.
pieces: Now the end is upon you. I will unleash {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger against you, judge you by your ways, and bring all your detestable practices down on you.

L.3: Now the end [is] upon you, and I will send {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger against you, and I will judge you according to your ways, and I will lay upon you all your abominations.

R.3: Now the end has come for you. I will turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger loose on you. I will judge you for the way you have lived and punish you for all the disgusting things you have done.

decisions.choice: I will lay upon you all your abominations: you will bear the consequences of what you have done
decisions.reason: To lay someone's deeds upon them is to make them carry their consequences. The LORD's judgment is not arbitrary: it gives back to the people what their own conduct has earned (verses 4, 8-9, 27; 9:10; 11:21).

decisions.choice: you: the land and its people
decisions.reason: The "you" in verses 3-9 is feminine singular, the land of Israel addressed as a woman (verse 2), and through her its people.

decisions.choice: anger (L, B, R); abominations / detestable practices / disgusting things
decisions.reason: *'Af* is "anger" at every level, and *to'evah* follows 5:9. Balanced says "bring ... down on you" and Readable "punish you for", the sense of the idiom in m1.

records.source: וְלֹא־תָח֥וֹס עֵינִ֛י עָלַ֖יִךְ וְלֹ֣א אֶחְמ֑וֹל כִּ֣י דְרָכַ֜יִךְ עָלַ֣יִךְ אֶתֵּ֗ן וְתוֹעֲבוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ בְּתוֹכֵ֣ךְ תִּֽהְיֶ֔יןָ וִידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And not will pity my eye on you, and not I will spare; for your ways on you I will lay, and your abominations in your midst will be, and you will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: I will not look on you with pity or spare you. I will bring your ways down on you, and your detestable practices will remain among you. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.4: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eye will not pity you, and I will not spare; for I will lay your ways upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst; and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.4: I will not feel sorry for you or show you mercy. I will punish you for the way you have lived, and the disgusting things you do will stay among you and bring their punishment. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: your abominations will be in your midst: their consequences will stay with you
alternatives: your idols will remain among you, powerless
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean that the punishment their practices deserve will come home to them, or that the idols they served will be left among them, unable to help. The first fits the parallel "I will lay your ways upon you".

decisions.choice: my eye will not pity, and I will not spare (L); I will not look on you with pity or spare you (B); I will not feel sorry for you or show you mercy (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set at 5:11 for this phrase, and the refrain as set at 6:7 ("Then you will know that I am the LORD"). Readable adds "and bring their punishment" for the sense taken in m1.

records.source: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה רָעָ֛ה אַחַ֥ת רָעָ֖ה הִנֵּ֥ה בָאָֽה׃
records.gloss: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Disaster, one disaster, see, it is coming!
pieces: The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: Disaster! A disaster unlike any other! See, it is coming!

L.5: Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: Disaster! A single disaster! See, it is coming!

R.5: This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: Disaster! A disaster like no other is coming!

decisions.choice: a single disaster: one disaster, unique
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "disaster, one disaster": a disaster that stands alone, unlike any other (compare 5:9), or one blow that finishes everything. Many Hebrew manuscripts and the Targum read a word that differs by one similar letter, "after": "disaster after disaster", which matches 7:26.

decisions.choice: A single disaster (L); unlike any other (B); like no other (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "one"; Balanced and Readable say what it means here (m1). The formula follows 2:4.

records.source: קֵ֣ץ בָּ֔א בָּ֥א הַקֵּ֖ץ הֵקִ֣יץ אֵלָ֑יִךְ הִנֵּ֖ה בָּאָֽה׃
records.gloss: An end has come; has come the end; it has awakened against you; see, it is coming!
pieces: An end has come! The end has come! It has woken up against you. See, it is coming!

L.6: An end has come; the end has come; it has awakened against you; see, it is coming!

R.6: The end has come! The end has come! It has woken up and is coming for you! Here it comes!

decisions.choice: the end ... has awakened: a play on words
decisions.reason: "End" and "has awakened" sound alike in Hebrew, as "summer fruit" and "end" did in Amos 8:2. The end is pictured as something that has been asleep and now rises against the land.

decisions.choice: it has awakened (L); It has woken up (B, R)
decisions.reason: The play on words cannot be kept in English; the footnote gives it.

records.source: בָּ֧אָה הַצְּפִירָ֛ה אֵלֶ֖יךָ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב הָאָ֑רֶץ בָּ֣א הָעֵ֗ת קָר֛וֹב הַיּ֥וֹם מְהוּמָ֖ה וְלֹא־הֵ֥ד הָרִֽים׃
records.gloss: Has come the doom to you, inhabitant of the land; has come the time, near [is] the day; tumult, and not shouting, [on the] mountains.
pieces: Doom has come to you who live in the land. The time has come, the day is close at hand: panic on the mountains, not shouts of joy.

L.7: The doom has come to you, you who dwell in the land; the time has come, near is the day: tumult, and not joyful shouting, on the mountains.

R.7: Your doom has come, you people who live in the land. The time has come. The day is near. There will be panic on the mountains, not happy shouting.

decisions.choice: the doom: the word is uncertain
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here, in verse 10 and in Isaiah 28:5, where it means a crown or garland. Here it seems to mean what comes round in turn, one's fate or doom, or the dawn of the day of judgment. The sense of something fateful arriving is clear from the context.

decisions.choice: tumult, and not joyful shouting: panic instead of harvest songs
decisions.reason: The second word is the shout of those treading grapes at harvest (Isaiah 16:10; Jeremiah 25:30; 48:33). On the mountains, where the vineyards and the shrines were, there will be the noise of panic instead.

decisions.choice: the time has come, the day is near: the day of the LORD
decisions.reason: "The day" is the day of the LORD's judgment that the prophets announced (Amos 5:18-20; Zephaniah 1:14). Ezekiel 30:3 uses the same words: "the day is near, the day of the LORD is near".

decisions.choice: you who live in the land (B); you people who live in the land (R)
decisions.reason: "Inhabitant" is singular in Hebrew, standing for all who live in the land; Balanced and Readable say it as English would.

records.source: עַתָּ֣ה מִקָּר֗וֹב אֶשְׁפּ֤וֹךְ חֲמָתִי֙ עָלַ֔יִךְ וְכִלֵּיתִ֤י אַפִּי֙ בָּ֔ךְ וּשְׁפַטְתִּ֖יךְ כִּדְרָכָ֑יִךְ וְנָתַתִּ֣י עָלַ֔יִךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־תּוֹעֲבוֹתָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: Now from near I will pour out my wrath on you, and I will complete my anger against you, and I will judge you according to your ways, and I will lay on you all your abominations.
pieces: Very soon I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath on you and spend {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger against you. I will judge you by your ways and bring all your detestable practices down on you.

L.8: Now shortly I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath upon you, and I will spend {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger against you, and I will judge you according to your ways, and I will lay upon you all your abominations.

R.8: Very soon I will pour out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger on you. I will let all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger loose against you. I will judge you for the way you have lived and punish you for all the disgusting things you have done.

decisions.choice: verses 8-9 repeat verses 3-4: a refrain
decisions.reason: Verses 8-9 repeat verses 3-4 almost word for word, adding "I will pour out my wrath" and, at the end, "the LORD who strikes". The repetition hammers home the certainty of the judgment.

decisions.choice: wrath, anger (L, B); anger (R)
decisions.reason: *Chemah* is "wrath" at Literal and Balanced and "anger" at Readable; *'af* is "anger" at every level, as in 5:13. The rest repeats the wording of verse 3 at each level.

records.source: וְלֹא־תָח֥וֹס עֵינִ֖י וְלֹ֣א אֶחְמ֑וֹל כִּדְרָכַ֜יִךְ עָלַ֣יִךְ אֶתֵּ֗ן וְתוֹעֲבוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ בְּתוֹכֵ֣ךְ תִּֽהְיֶ֔יןָ וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מַכֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And not will pity my eye, and not I will spare; according to your ways on you I will lay, and your abominations in your midst will be, and you will know that I [am] Yahweh, striking.
pieces: I will not look on you with pity or spare you. I will bring your ways down on you, and your detestable practices will remain among you. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the one who strikes.

L.9: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eye will not pity, and I will not spare; according to your ways I will lay [it] upon you, and your abominations will be in your midst; and you will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who strikes.

R.9: I will not feel sorry for you or show you mercy. I will punish you for the way you have lived, and the disgusting things you do will stay among you and bring their punishment. Then you will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the one who is striking you.

decisions.choice: you will know that I am the LORD, who strikes: the LORD known in his blows
decisions.reason: The refrain of 6:7 is extended: the people will know the LORD as the one who strikes them. The disaster is not chance or the work of Babylon's gods; it is the LORD's own hand, as he says in Deuteronomy 32:39, "I wound and I heal".

decisions.choice: and you will know that I [am] the LORD, who strikes (L); Then you will know that I am the LORD, the one who strikes (B, R)
decisions.reason: The refrain as set at 6:7, with the added word. The rest repeats the wording of verse 4 at each level.

records.source: הִנֵּ֥ה הַיּ֖וֹם הִנֵּ֣ה בָאָ֑ה יָֽצְאָה֙ הַצְּפִרָ֔ה צָ֚ץ הַמַּטֶּ֔ה פָּרַ֖ח הַזָּדֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: See, the day! See, it is coming! Has gone out the doom; has blossomed the rod; has budded the arrogance.
pieces: See, the day! See, it is coming! Doom has gone out. The rod has blossomed; arrogance has sprouted.

L.10: See, the day! See, it is coming! The doom has gone out; the rod has blossomed; arrogance has budded.

R.10: Look! The day is coming! Doom has come out. The rod is in bloom, and pride has sprouted.

decisions.choice: the rod has blossomed, arrogance has budded: wickedness is ripe for judgment
alternatives: the arrogance of Babylon, the rod of punishment
decisions.reason: The picture is of a plant coming into flower. The "rod" may be the rod of punishment, the Babylonian power the LORD will use (as Assyria is "the rod of my anger" in Isaiah 10:5), or it may be Israel's own arrogance and violence (verse 11), now ripe and ready for the harvest of judgment. The word can also mean a staff or scepter. The budding rod recalls Aaron's staff that blossomed (Numbers 17:23), here turned into a sign of doom.

decisions.choice: is in bloom, has sprouted (R)
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture of the plant. *Tsefirah*, "doom", is as in verse 7.

records.source: הֶחָמָ֥ס׀קָ֖ם לְמַטֵּה־רֶ֑שַׁע לֹא־מֵהֶ֞ם וְלֹ֧א מֵהֲמוֹנָ֛ם וְלֹ֥א מֶהֱמֵהֶ֖ם וְלֹא־נֹ֥הַּ בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: The violence has risen to a rod of wickedness; not of them, and not of their multitude, and not of their wealth, and not eminence among them.
pieces: Violence has grown into a rod to punish wickedness. None of them will be left, none of their crowds, none of their wealth, and nothing of worth among them.

L.11: Violence has grown up into a rod of wickedness. Nothing [will be left] of them, nor of their multitude, nor of their wealth; and there is no eminence among them.

R.11: Violence has grown into a rod to punish evil. Nothing will be left of the people, their crowds or their riches. Nothing of value will be left among them.

decisions.choice: violence has grown up into a rod of wickedness: the people's violence brings its own punishment
alternatives: violence has grown up into a wicked rod
decisions.reason: The people's violence has grown, like the rod of verse 10, into a rod that punishes wickedness; or the violence itself is a wicked rod. The words are terse and the exact sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: their wealth ... eminence: rare words
decisions.reason: Both words are rare. The first may mean their wealth, or their noise and bustle; the second, which occurs only here, may mean eminence or splendor, or perhaps wailing for the dead ("no one will mourn them"). The sense of the line is that nothing and no one will be left.

decisions.choice: a rod to punish wickedness (B, R); will be left (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable take the reading in m1 and say "to punish". The Hebrew has no verb in the second half; "will be left" is supplied, bracketed at Literal.

records.source: בָּ֤א הָעֵת֙ הִגִּ֣יעַ הַיּ֔וֹם הַקּוֹנֶה֙ אַל־יִשְׂמָ֔ח וְהַמּוֹכֵ֖ר אַל־יִתְאַבָּ֑ל כִּ֥י חָר֖וֹן אֶל־כָּל־הֲמוֹנָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: Has come the time; has arrived the day; the buyer let him not rejoice, and the seller let him not mourn, for burning [anger is] against all its multitude.
pieces: The time has come; the day is here. The buyer should not rejoice, nor the seller grieve, for fierce anger is coming on all its crowds.

L.12: The time has come; the day has drawn near. Let the buyer not rejoice, and let the seller not mourn, for burning [anger is] against all its multitude.

R.12: The time has come. The day is here. People who buy land should not be happy, and people who sell it should not be sad, for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger is coming on everyone in the land.

decisions.choice: the buyer and the seller: property no longer matters
decisions.reason: Land in Israel was held by families, and a family that sold land under pressure hoped to get it back (Leviticus 25:13-28). Now neither the buyer's gain nor the seller's loss means anything, because all will lose the land together. Jeremiah bought a field during the siege as a sign of the opposite hope (Jeremiah 32:6-15).

decisions.choice: burning anger against all its multitude: the LORD's anger against the whole land
decisions.reason: The word means burning or fierce anger, the LORD's (verse 14 says "my burning anger"). "Its multitude" is the crowds of the land.

decisions.choice: my anger (R); land (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says whose anger it is, from verse 14, and "buy land" for what was bought and sold (m1). *Charon* is "burning anger" at Literal and "fierce anger" at Balanced.

records.source: כִּ֣י הַמּוֹכֵ֗ר אֶל־הַמִּמְכָּר֙ לֹ֣א יָשׁ֔וּב וְע֥וֹד בַּחַיִּ֖ים חַיָּתָ֑ם כִּֽי־חָז֤וֹן אֶל־כָּל־הֲמוֹנָהּ֙ לֹ֣א יָשׁ֔וּב וְאִ֧ישׁ בַּעֲוֺנ֛וֹ חַיָּת֖וֹ לֹ֥א יִתְחַזָּֽקוּ׃
records.gloss: For the seller to the thing sold not will return, while still in life [is] their life; for [the] vision [is] concerning all its multitude, it will not turn back; and [each] man in his iniquity his life not they will strengthen.
pieces: Sellers will not get back what they sold, even if they are still alive, for the vision concerning all its crowds will not be revoked. Because of their sin, not one of them will hold on to life.

L.13: For the seller will not return to what was sold, while their life [is] still among the living; for the vision concerning all its multitude will not turn back; and no one, in {{gender:their|his}} iniquity, will hold on to {{gender:their|his}} life.

R.13: Those who sell will never get back what they sold, even if they live, because the vision about all the people will not be taken back. Because of their sins, none of them will save their own lives.

decisions.choice: the seller will not return to what was sold: no year of release
decisions.reason: Under the law of the jubilee, land that had been sold went back to its family (Leviticus 25:13, 28). The exile will cancel that hope: the seller will not get the land back in their lifetime.

decisions.choice: the vision will not turn back ... no one will hold on to life: a hard verse
decisions.reason: The second half of the verse is obscure. Some of its words seem to repeat verse 12, and the Greek translation is shorter here. The general sense is that the vision of judgment will not be withdrawn, and that no one, sinful as they are, will be able to keep their life.

decisions.choice: their / his (gender setting)
decisions.reason: "Each man" here means anyone, so Literal gives the pronouns through the gender setting; Balanced and Readable use plurals. Balanced says "revoked" and Readable "taken back" for "will not turn back".

records.source: תָּקְע֤וּ בַתָּק֨וֹעַ֙ וְהָכִ֣ין הַכֹּ֔ל וְאֵ֥ין הֹלֵ֖ךְ לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה כִּ֥י חֲרוֹנִ֖י אֶל־כָּל־הֲמוֹנָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: They have blown on the trumpet and prepared everything, and there is no [one] going to the battle, for my burning [anger is] against all its multitude.
pieces: They have sounded the trumpet and made everything ready, but no one goes out to fight, for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fierce anger is on all its crowds.

L.14: They have blown the trumpet and prepared everything, but there is no one going to the battle, for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} burning [anger is] against all its multitude.

R.14: They blow the trumpet and get everything ready for war. But no one goes out to fight, because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger is against all of them.

decisions.choice: the trumpet: a horn sounded to call men to battle
decisions.reason: The word for the instrument occurs only here; it comes from the verb "to blow". It is the alarm that calls the army out. But fear has taken their strength (verse 17), and no one answers the call.

decisions.choice: trumpet (L, B, R); burning anger (L); fierce anger (B); anger (R)
decisions.reason: "Trumpet" at every level, since the word is not the usual one for the ram's horn. *Charon* follows verse 12.

records.source: הַחֶ֣רֶב בַּח֔וּץ וְהַדֶּ֥בֶר וְהָרָעָ֖ב מִבָּ֑יִת אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּשָּׂדֶה֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב יָמ֔וּת וַאֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּעִ֔יר רָעָ֥ב וָדֶ֖בֶר יֹאכֲלֶֽנּוּ׃
records.gloss: The sword [is] outside, and the pestilence and the famine inside; [the one] who [is] in the field by the sword will die, and [the one] who [is] in the city, famine and pestilence will devour him.
pieces: The sword is outside, plague and famine inside. Whoever is in the countryside will die by the sword, and whoever is in the city will be devoured by famine and plague.

L.15: The sword [is] outside, and pestilence and famine inside; the one who [is] in the field will die by the sword, and the one who [is] in the city, famine and pestilence will devour {{gender:them|him}}.

R.15: War is outside the city, and disease and hunger are inside. People in the countryside will be killed in battle, and people in the city will die of hunger and disease.

decisions.choice: the sword outside and pestilence and famine inside: no place is safe
decisions.reason: The same picture is in Jeremiah 14:18 and Lamentations 1:20 ("outside the sword bereaves; inside it is like death"), and in Deuteronomy 32:25. The three judgments are those of 5:12.

decisions.choice: sword, pestilence, famine (L); sword, plague, famine (B); war, disease, hunger (R)
decisions.reason: The Jeremiah wording, as in 5:12. The one in the city stands for anyone, so Literal's pronoun takes the gender setting.

records.source: וּפָֽלְטוּ֙ פְּלִ֣יטֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָי֣וּ אֶל־הֶהָרִ֗ים כְּיוֹנֵ֧י הַגֵּאָי֛וֹת כֻּלָּ֖ם הֹמ֑וֹת אִ֖ישׁ בַּעֲוֺנֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And will escape their escapees, and they will be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, [each] man in his iniquity.
pieces: Any who escape will flee to the mountains and be like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each over {{gender:their|his}} own sin.

L.16: And their survivors will escape, and they will be on the mountains like the doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each for {{gender:their|his}} iniquity.

R.16: Those who escape will run away to the mountains. They will moan like doves from the valleys, each one groaning over {{gender:their|his}} own sins.

decisions.choice: like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning: the sound of grief
decisions.reason: The low call of the dove was heard as moaning (Isaiah 38:14; 59:11; Nahum 2:8). Doves that nest in the valleys flee to the mountains; so the survivors will hide in the hills, grieving over their sin.

decisions.choice: their / his (gender setting)
decisions.reason: "Each man" means each person, so the pronoun takes the gender setting. *'Awon* is "iniquity" at Literal and "sin" at Balanced and Readable.

records.source: כָּל־הַיָּדַ֖יִם תִּרְפֶּ֑ינָה וְכָל־בִּרְכַּ֖יִם תֵּלַ֥כְנָה מָּֽיִם׃
records.gloss: All the hands will hang limp, and all knees will go water.
pieces: Every hand will hang limp, and every knee will turn to water.

L.17: All hands will hang limp, and all knees will go [as] water.

R.17: Everyone's hands will hang down weak, and their knees will be as weak as water.

decisions.choice: all knees will go as water: weakness from terror
alternatives: their knees will be wet with urine
decisions.reason: Limp hands and watery knees describe people too terrified to act or stand (21:12; Isaiah 13:7). The Hebrew says the knees "will go water": that is, become weak as water, or, as some take it, be wet with urine from fear. The words are kept close to the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: every knee will turn to water (B); as weak as water (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the English idiom for weakness from fear, which is close to the Hebrew picture; Readable says it plainly. The footnote gives the other reading.

records.source: וְחָגְר֣וּ שַׂקִּ֔ים וְכִסְּתָ֥ה אוֹתָ֖ם פַּלָּצ֑וּת וְאֶ֤ל כָּל־פָּנִים֙ בּוּשָׁ֔ה וּבְכָל־רָאשֵׁיהֶ֖ם קָרְחָֽה׃
records.gloss: And they will gird on sackcloth, and will cover them shuddering; and to every face [will be] shame, and on all their heads baldness.
pieces: They will put on sackcloth and be covered with terror. Shame will be on every face, and every head will be shaved.

L.18: And they will put on sackcloth, and shuddering will cover them; and on every face [will be] shame, and on all their heads baldness.

R.18: They will dress in rough sackcloth to show their grief, and they will shake with fear. Everyone's face will show their shame, and they will shave their heads in mourning.

decisions.choice: sackcloth and baldness: the signs of mourning
decisions.reason: Sackcloth was coarse cloth of goat's hair worn in mourning and repentance, and shaving the head was a sign of grief (Isaiah 15:2-3; Amos 8:10; compare 5:1). The whole people will be in mourning.

decisions.choice: to show their grief; in mourning (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the sackcloth and shaved heads meant (m1).

records.source: כַּסְפָּ֞ם בַּחוּצ֣וֹת יַשְׁלִ֗יכוּ וּזְהָבָם֮ לְנִדָּ֣ה יִֽהְיֶה֒ כַּסְפָּ֨ם וּזְהָבָ֜ם לֹֽא־יוּכַ֣ל לְהַצִּילָ֗ם בְּיוֹם֙ עֶבְרַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה נַפְשָׁם֙ לֹ֣א יְשַׂבֵּ֔עוּ וּמֵעֵיהֶ֖ם לֹ֣א יְמַלֵּ֑אוּ כִּֽי־מִכְשׁ֥וֹל עֲוֺנָ֖ם הָיָֽה׃
records.gloss: Their silver in the streets they will throw, and their gold an impurity will become; their silver and their gold not will be able to deliver them in [the] day of [the] fury of Yahweh; their appetite not they will satisfy, and their stomachs not they will fill, for [the] stumbling block of their iniquity it has become.
pieces: Their silver they will fling into the streets, and their gold will be something unclean. Their silver and their gold will not be able to save them on the day of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s fury. It cannot satisfy their hunger or fill their stomachs, for it made them stumble into sin.

L.19: Their silver they will throw into the streets, and their gold will become an impurity. Their silver and their gold will not be able to rescue them on the day of the fury of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. They will not satisfy their hunger or fill their stomachs, for it has been the stumbling block of their iniquity.

R.19: They will throw away their silver in the streets, and their gold will be like something unclean. Their silver and gold will not be able to save them on the day when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shows {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger. It cannot buy them food or fill their stomachs, for it was what led them into sin.

decisions.choice: their silver and their gold will not be able to rescue them on the day of the fury of the LORD: Zephaniah 1:18
decisions.reason: Zephaniah says almost the same words: "Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to rescue them on the day of the fury of the LORD" (Zephaniah 1:18). On the day of judgment wealth is worthless.

decisions.choice: an impurity: something unclean, to be thrown away
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for the impurity of a woman's monthly period (Leviticus 15:19-24) and then for anything unclean that must be put away (Lamentations 1:8, 17). Gold, which they used to make their idols (verse 20), will be thrown away like something unclean (Isaiah 30:22).

decisions.choice: the stumbling block of their iniquity: what made them fall into sin
decisions.reason: Their wealth tripped them up and made them sin, for they made idols from it (verse 20). The phrase returns in 14:3-7 and 18:30.

decisions.choice: the wording of Zephaniah 1:18 at each level
decisions.reason: The line repeats Zephaniah 1:18, so it reuses the published wording at each level: "will not be able to rescue them on the day of the fury of the LORD" (L), "will not be able to save them on the day of the LORD's fury" (B), "will not be able to save them on the day when the LORD shows his anger" (R). Zephaniah begins "Neither ... nor", where Ezekiel has "their silver and their gold", which each level keeps. Readable says "buy them food" for satisfying their hunger.

records.source: וּצְבִ֤י עֶדְיוֹ֙ לְגָא֣וֹן שָׂמָ֔הוּ וְצַלְמֵ֧י תוֹעֲבֹתָ֛ם שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֖ם עָ֣שׂוּ ב֑וֹ עַל־כֵּ֛ן נְתַתִּ֥יו לָהֶ֖ם לְנִדָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And [the] beauty of his ornament into pride he set it, and [the] images of their abominations, their detestable things, they made with it; therefore I will make it to them an impurity.
pieces: They took pride in their beautiful jewelry and used it to make the images of their detestable practices and their vile idols. Therefore I will make it something unclean to them.

L.20: And the beauty of its ornament—he turned it into pride, and the images of their abominations, their detestable things, they made with it; therefore I will make it an impurity to them.

R.20: They were proud of their beautiful jewelry, and they used it to make their disgusting idols. So I will make their gold and silver disgusting to them.

decisions.choice: the beauty of its ornament: their gold and silver jewelry
alternatives: the temple, the LORD's beautiful ornament
decisions.reason: In the setting of verse 19, "the beauty of its ornament" is their jewelry of gold and silver, which they were proud of and from which they made idols, as Israel made the golden calf from its earrings (Exodus 32:2-4; Hosea 8:4). Some take it as the temple, the LORD's beautiful ornament, which is profaned in verses 21-22.

decisions.choice: abominations, detestable things (L); detestable practices, vile idols (B); disgusting idols (R)
decisions.reason: *To'evah* follows 5:9 and *shiqqutsim* 5:11. Readable puts the two into one phrase. Literal keeps "he" for the people as one; Balanced and Readable say "they".

records.source: וּנְתַתִּ֤יו בְּיַֽד־הַזָּרִים֙ לָבַ֔ז וּלְרִשְׁעֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ לְשָׁלָ֑ל וְחִלְּלֽוּהוּ׃
records.gloss: And I will give it into [the] hand of the strangers for plunder, and to [the] wicked of the earth for spoil, and they will profane it.
pieces: I will hand it over as plunder to foreigners and as spoil to the wicked of the earth, and they will profane it.

L.21: And I will give it into the hand of strangers for plunder, and to the wicked of the earth for spoil, and they will profane it.

R.21: I will give their riches to foreigners as loot, to wicked people from other lands, and they will treat it as something worthless.

decisions.choice: they will profane it: the reading tradition
decisions.reason: The written form of the verb has a masculine object, "him" or "it"; the scribes' marginal note reads a feminine "it". The sense is not changed: the plunderers will treat what was holy as common.

decisions.choice: profane: treat what is holy as common
decisions.reason: To profane is to treat something set apart for God as ordinary. The verb is repeated in verses 21-22 and 24: the wealth that was dedicated, the LORD's treasured place, and the sanctuaries will all be profaned by foreigners.

decisions.choice: treat it as something worthless (R)
decisions.reason: Readable gives a plain sense of "profane"; Literal and Balanced keep the word.

records.source: וַהֲסִבּוֹתִ֤י פָנַי֙ מֵהֶ֔ם וְחִלְּל֖וּ אֶת־צְפוּנִ֑י וּבָאוּ־בָ֥הּ פָּרִיצִ֖ים וְחִלְּלֽוּהָ׃פ
records.gloss: And I will turn my face from them, and they will profane my treasured [place], and will enter into it robbers and profane it.
pieces: I will turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face away from them, and they will profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} treasured place. Robbers will break into it and defile it.

L.22: And I will turn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} face from them, and they will profane {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} treasured [place]; and robbers will enter it and profane it.

R.22: I will turn away from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people, and foreigners will make {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} treasured place unclean. Robbers will break into it and treat it with contempt.

decisions.choice: my treasured place: probably the temple
decisions.reason: The word means something hidden or treasured. It is most likely the temple, the LORD's precious possession, perhaps its innermost room; chapters 8-11 show the LORD leaving it. Some take it as the land, or the treasures kept in the temple.

decisions.choice: I will turn my face from them: the LORD withdraws his protection
decisions.reason: To turn the face away is to stop looking on someone with favor and to leave them unprotected (39:23-24; Deuteronomy 31:17).

decisions.choice: foreigners (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names those who profane it, from verse 21, and "my people" for "them".

records.source: עֲשֵׂ֖ה הָֽרַתּ֑וֹק כִּ֣י הָאָ֗רֶץ מָֽלְאָה֙ מִשְׁפַּ֣ט דָּמִ֔ים וְהָעִ֖יר מָלְאָ֥ה חָמָֽס׃
records.gloss: Make the chain, for the land is full of judgment of bloods, and the city is full of violence.
pieces: Make a chain! For the land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of violence.

L.23: Make the chain! For the land is full of bloody judgment, and the city is full of violence.

R.23: Get chains ready for prisoners! For the land is full of murder, and the city is full of violence.

decisions.choice: the chain: chains for captives
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here, and its sense is uncertain. It is usually taken as a chain, the kind used to lead prisoners into exile (Nahum 3:10; Jeremiah 40:1). The command may be another sign-act for Ezekiel, or a cry to the enemy. The Greek translation reads differently, and some take the word as a verb of confusion.

decisions.choice: judgment of bloods: crimes of bloodshed
decisions.reason: The phrase means crimes that deserve the death sentence, the shedding of innocent blood (22:2-4). The land is full of murder and the city of violence, as the earth was before the flood (Genesis 6:11-13).

decisions.choice: bloodshed (B); murder (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "bloody judgment"; Balanced and Readable say what the phrase means (m2). Readable adds "for prisoners" for the use of the chain (m1).

records.heading: Make a chain

records.source: וְהֵֽבֵאתִי֙ רָעֵ֣י גוֹיִ֔ם וְיָרְשׁ֖וּ אֶת־בָּֽתֵּיהֶ֑ם וְהִשְׁבַּתִּי֙ גְּא֣וֹן עַזִּ֔ים וְנִחֲל֖וּ מְקַֽדְשֵׁיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And I will bring [the] worst of [the] nations, and they will possess their houses; and I will make cease [the] pride of [the] strong, and will be profaned their holy places.
pieces: I will bring the most evil of the nations to take over their houses. I will put an end to the pride of the powerful, and their holy places will be defiled.

L.24: And I will bring the worst of the nations, and they will take possession of their houses; and I will make the pride of the strong cease, and their holy places will be profaned.

R.24: I will bring the cruelest nations to take over their houses. I will put an end to the pride of the powerful, and their places of worship will be made unclean.

decisions.choice: the worst of the nations: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: The phrase names the most evil and ruthless of nations; in 28:7 and 30:11 it is the Babylonian army of Nebuchadnezzar.

decisions.choice: their holy places: their sanctuaries
decisions.reason: The plural may mean the temple and its courts, or the local shrines; the form could also be read "those who make them holy". It is taken as "their holy places".

decisions.choice: the most evil of the nations (B); the cruelest nations (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "most evil" and "cruelest" for "the worst".

records.source: קְפָ֖דָה־בָ֑א וּבִקְשׁ֥וּ שָׁל֖וֹם וָאָֽיִן׃
records.gloss: Anguish has come, and they will seek peace, and there is none.
pieces: Terror is coming! They will look for peace, but there will be none.

L.25: Anguish is coming, and they will seek peace, but there will be none.

R.25: Terror is coming. They will look for peace, but they will not find it.

decisions.choice: anguish: terror, shuddering
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It is related to a verb for rolling up or shrinking together, and seems to mean anguish or terror.

decisions.choice: they will seek peace, but there will be none: the false hope of peace
decisions.reason: The prophets who said "Peace" when there was no peace (Jeremiah 6:14; 8:11; Ezekiel 13:10, 16) will be proved wrong.

decisions.choice: peace (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: *Shalom* is "peace" at every level, as in Isaiah.

records.source: הֹוָ֤ה עַל־הֹוָה֙ תָּב֔וֹא וּשְׁמֻעָ֥ה אֶל־שְׁמוּעָ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶ֑ה וּבִקְשׁ֤וּ חָזוֹן֙ מִנָּבִ֔יא וְתוֹרָה֙ תֹּאבַ֣ד מִכֹּהֵ֔ן וְעֵצָ֖ה מִזְּקֵנִֽים׃
records.gloss: Disaster upon disaster will come, and report upon report will be, and they will seek a vision from a prophet, and instruction will perish from [the] priest, and counsel from [the] elders.
pieces: Disaster will follow disaster, and rumor will follow rumor. They will seek a vision from a prophet, but the priest will have no instruction to give, and the elders no counsel.

L.26: Disaster upon disaster will come, and report upon report will be; and they will seek a vision from a prophet, but instruction will perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.

R.26: One disaster will follow another, and one bad report will follow another. People will ask a prophet for a vision. But the priests will have no teaching to give, and the elders will have no advice.

decisions.choice: instruction will perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders: Jeremiah 18:18 reversed
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's enemies said, "Instruction will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet" (Jeremiah 18:18). Ezekiel says that all three will fail. Lamentations 2:9 says the same of the fallen city.

decisions.choice: disaster ... report: one blow after another
decisions.reason: The first word means ruin or disaster (Isaiah 47:11); the second, a report or piece of news. Bad news will arrive on top of bad news.

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B); teaching (R)
decisions.reason: *Torah* is "instruction" at Literal and Balanced and "teaching" at Readable, as in Isaiah and Jeremiah.

records.source: הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ יִתְאַבָּ֗ל וְנָשִׂיא֙ יִלְבַּ֣שׁ שְׁמָמָ֔ה וִידֵ֥י עַם־הָאָ֖רֶץ תִּבָּהַ֑לְנָה מִדַּרְכָּ֞ם אֶעֱשֶׂ֤ה אוֹתָם֙ וּבְמִשְׁפְּטֵיהֶ֣ם אֶשְׁפְּטֵ֔ם וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: The king will mourn, and [the] prince will wear desolation, and the hands of [the] people of the land will tremble; from their way I will deal with them, and by their judgments I will judge them, and they will know that I [am] Yahweh.
pieces: The king will mourn, the prince will be clothed in despair, and the hands of the people of the land will shake with fear. I will deal with them according to their ways and judge them by the standards they themselves use. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.27: The king will mourn, and the prince will wear desolation, and the hands of the people of the land will tremble. According to their way I will deal with them, and by their own judgments I will judge them; and they will know that I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.27: The king will mourn, the ruler will be filled with despair, and the people of the land will tremble with fear. I will punish them for the way they have lived, and judge them by the standards they used on others. Then they will know that I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the king ... the prince: the rulers of Judah
decisions.reason: Ezekiel often calls the king of Judah "prince" rather than "king" (12:10, 12; 21:30). Here both words stand side by side for the rulers, from the king down; the Greek translation lacks "the king will mourn". "The people of the land" are the landholding citizens of Judah.

decisions.choice: by their own judgments I will judge them: the punishment fits the deeds
decisions.reason: The LORD will deal with them by the standards they themselves used, as Jesus says, "with the judgment you pronounce you will be judged" (Matthew 7:2).

decisions.choice: prince (L, B); ruler (R); and they will know that I [am] the LORD (L); Then they will know that I am the LORD (B, R)
decisions.reason: *Nasi'* follows the Ezekiel table: "prince" at Literal and Balanced, "ruler" at Readable. The refrain is as set at 6:7, with "they".
